explanation: The apostle who traveled to Jerusalem was attacked by a conspiracy and later escorted to Caesarea.
A secret pact among Jews in Jerusalem who swore not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
The Roman officer (Claudius Lysias) who rescued Paul from the crowd and took him under protection.
The Jewish council body in Jerusalem where Paul was brought to be questioned about his beliefs.
The sect of Jews (the Pharisees) who believed in the resurrection, which created disagreement with the Sadducees during the hearing.
Another group in the Jewish council who did not believe in the resurrection or angels, and thus became divided from the Pharisees.
The capital of the Roman province of Judea where Paul was sent for safety under guard by soldiers.
The Roman governor (Felix) who received the case against Paul and held him in custody.
